_what: Every way our macro expansion differs from the game's own, for the whole scenario pool. Regenerate with `python tools/analysis/expansion_diff.py --write-expected`, and read the diff before committing it: a NEW entry means our expander and Wesnoth disagree about a scenario, which is a bug until classified.

_classifications.SUBSTITUTED: The behaviour is real and the sim implements it itself, so the WML body is dropped deliberately. `stands_in` names the code that must not be deleted without putting the macro back.
_classifications.IGNORED: Presentation only; nothing downstream reads it.

event count | prestart: ours 0, the game.why: The era's [lua] prestart calling quick_4mp_leaders (wesnoth_src/data/multiplayer/eras.lua:5-22): every leader with max_moves=4 gains the quick trait at scenario start. Our expander emits no [lua], and the sim applies the same rule natively while rolling a leader's traits, so the behaviour is present and the WML body is not. The substitution is NOT the whole macro: the era gates it on the WML variable `make_4mp_leaders_quick` and skips any unit whose own `dont_make_me_quick` variable is set (eras.lua:6-16), and tools/traits.py reads neither. That is exact only because no scenario we build touches either gate -- checked over the pool and the two off-whitelist corpus maps by tests/test_wml_state.py, and enforced at build time by wml_state.check_quick_leader_gates. Dark Forecast and Isle of Mists DO set dont_make_me_quick, so the gates are real; those maps are simply not ours.
